conventions.width: Width comes from the data-type column. U32/S32 are two consecutive registers, low word first.
conventions.kind: The decoder vocabulary shared with the hybrid and PV maps: u16, s16, u32, s32, ascii, bit. Says WIDTH and SIGNEDNESS in one field, so a register the document mislabels can be corrected by an override without touching data_type, which records what the document actually printed. conventions.word_order: 32-bit registers are LITTLE-endian (low word first) — the opposite of PV. Stated in each register's own description and confirmed against a live 3-phase capture on 2026-08-07.
conventions.precedence: overrides > app agreement > document (newest first). Both apps agree on every address, so conflicts here are app-vs-document or between the two apps' enum labels.

The extension's reading was winning before its config file stopped being harvested, and dropping it silently replaced all five labels. registers.note: Deliberately left WITHOUT units, and this is a decision, not a gap. 36011 is what the inverters report about THEMSELVES over the comms bus — their own real watts. It never passes through the EPM's CT clamps, so it must NOT be multiplied by CT or PT; doing so would inflate a already-correct figure by the CT ratio. The extension's transformer rule is units-driven, so an empty `units` string is exactly what keeps it unscaled. The app's own description map records kW, which is right for DISPLAY but must not be copied here, because here it would turn the multiply on. rule.title: FailSafe
rule.summary: A safety watchdog. The AX keeps checking its CTs (the clamps that measure current) and its other inputs. If anything looks wrong, it tells the inverters to drop to low generation.
rule.write_explain: Write the code directly, using the extension's numbering: 0 Off, 1 Normal, 2 Shutdown, 3 No Communication, 4 Force Limit. Tauri's labels for the same codes are believed wrong and are kept only in the conflict record.
rule.gotcha: This is protection, not an on/off switch. The AX keeps checking its CTs (the clamps that measure current) and its other inputs; if anything is wrong it tells the inverters to go to low generation. A fault must never let a site keep exporting freely. Tauri labels these same codes as ramp modes (Hard Limit / Ramp Down / Ramp Up / Ramp Both) — that reading is not trusted.

rule.title: Meter 1 select
rule.summary: One register holding two separate settings — the meter's make in the low byte, and where it is fitted in the high byte.
rule.write_explain: Read the register, change only the byte you mean to change, then write the whole word back. Writing a bare number clears the other byte.
rule.gotcha: Low byte is the meter type (0 Acrel, 1 Eastron, 2 Rayleigh, 3 Rayleigh F, 4 No Meter). High byte is where it sits (0 Grid, 1 Load, 2 Other PV, 3 Total PV, 4 Generator, 5 N/A). Writing '1' meaning 'Eastron' also sets the location to Grid, because the high byte becomes zero.
